overview: This one-page file item is an internal Department of State Solicitor’s Office memorandum considering whether the Department of Commerce should receive a copy of a consular despatch from Dairen and its enclosures concerning Japan’s promulgation of Ordinance No. 324, which governed industrial property in the Kwantung Leased Territory. It contrasts the practical value of the Dairen despatch with an attached Embassy despatch from Tokyo that treated the political implications, and recommends that the consular material alone would suffice if Commerce were to be notified. The referenced despatches and enclosures are not included in the supplied file text.

subfiles.title: Solicitor’s Office memorandum on transmitting industrial-property despatches to Commerce
subfiles.from: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Solicitor
subfiles.about: An internal memorandum asks whether the Department of Commerce should receive the Dairen consular despatch and enclosures concerning Japan’s Ordinance No. 324 for industrial property in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum notes that both a consular despatch from Dairen and an Embassy despatch from Tokyo discuss Japan’s promulgation of Ordinance No. 324. It distinguishes the Tokyo despatch as addressing the political phase of the issue. If the Department decides to inform Commerce, the writer suggests that sending the Dairen despatch and its enclosures would be sufficient. Routing initials and a February 18, 1930 receipt or action stamp appear on the page.

interest: The memorandum offers a compact view of how the State Department filtered overseas reporting for circulation to another federal department, separating the practical industrial-property material gathered at Dairen from the political analysis supplied by the Embassy in Tokyo. It is useful evidence of U.S. official attention to Japan’s extension of its legal and administrative regime into the Kwantung Leased Territory. The document also points to missing attachments that would likely contain the ordinance itself, its implementation details, and contemporary diplomatic analysis.
